data.hypothesis: A cyclic static schedule over whole scanlines should reduce dynamic pixel-chunk scheduling overhead while distributing vertically varying row costs more evenly than contiguous row blocks. A direct nested loop for one requested worker avoids OpenMP team overhead; pixel-keyed SplitMix64 streams keep each pixel's random sequence independent of schedule and thread count. This contrasts with the previously valid dynamic-64-pixel candidate; relative performance remains unmeasured.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use as a comparison point for the static scanline schedule; the available result is aggregate, not a per-configuration breakdown.
memory_lessons.claim: The dynamic pixel schedule with 64-pixel chunks and per-pixel SplitMix64 streams was controller-valid, with mean_seconds 0.46135 across three recorded times. This establishes correctness for that candidate, not a speed advantage for dynamic scheduling over static rows.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this static one-row cyclic schedule with repeated timings at every official performance configuration, including the one-worker case.

data.notes: No commands or local measurements were run. The prior dynamic-schedule candidate was correct on six correctness cases; this proposal changes the schedule and avoids per-pixel index division. The controller must determine correctness and repeated timings for all official performance configurations.
transformations: Replace shared worker-side random draws with a serial render seed and deterministic, pixel-keyed SplitMix64 streams.
Parallelize scanlines with OpenMP schedule(static, 1), assigning each row to one worker; each worker writes only its row's pixel triplets.
Use direct x/y coordinates in the pixel routine, avoiding flattened-index division while retaining the existing projection and ray loop structure.
Keep a direct serial nested loop when the requested worker count is one, and cap the OpenMP team with num_threads(worker_count).
Preserve nsubsamples squared primary samples and all 64 ambient rays at each hit; keep the existing ao_serial and run interfaces.
